claims.text: The 15–45 μm FeCoNiCrAl feedstock deposited by APS produces a bond coat below the required thickness.
Changing the feedstock particle-size distribution from 15–45 μm to 45–90 μm will increase the deposited coating thickness.
Increasing plasma-torch power can ensure complete melting of the 45–90 μm particles.
A mild inert preheating step could substitute for increased torch power in promoting full melting of the larger particles.
The modified process will retain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The 45–90 μm feedstock produces larger, higher-mass molten droplets than the 15–45 μm feedstock.
Fully molten larger droplets will flatten and coalesce into a thicker deposit.
Using larger particles avoids extended exposure to oxidation during deposition.
Larger particles have a lower surface-area-to-volume ratio.
The lower surface-area-to-volume ratio of larger particles causes greater retention of in-flight heat.
Larger particles experience shorter exposure to high-temperature oxidative environments.
Complete melting enhances formation of contiguous, well-adhered splats.
The modified process will produce a coating meeting or exceeding the design thickness while preserving coating integrity.
The intervention will remain effective under thermal-barrier-coating service conditions if melting is adequate and adverse microstructural and oxidation effects are avoided.

contradictions.description: The treatment is not defined consistently: the hypothesis specifies larger particles coupled with increased torch power, whereas the other fields allow either increased power or preheating. These are distinct interventions and are not isolated as separate experimental arms.
